correctness.rationale: For any congruence, restriction to zero bits respects semilattice join via the term-defined disjunction, while a projection term prevents mixed-bit identifications across different index congruence classes. Right multiplication by 1_j shows a collapsed class absorbs all quotient joins, hence must be greatest. The converse follows from quotient homomorphisms and a direct congruence check for the top two points. Inclusion is coordinatewise; finite semilattice quotients always have greatest element. Exhaustive direct checks corroborate 2,4,8,16,14,24 in six cases.

value.rationale: The natural construction I[2] realizes every bottom join-semilattice as a McCarthy skeleton, and complete knowledge of its quotients was not supplied by the source. This result classifies all congruences across arbitrary cardinalities, recovers the finite lattice exactly as Con(I)×2, gives a sharp infinite-case obstruction and counts quotients on every finite chain. It separates index collapse and Boolean-fiber collapse structurally rather than offering an arbitrary small enumeration.
